name: St. Gallen
flagName: Flag of the Canton of St. Gallen
summary: A green square with a white bundle of rods and an axe, the Roman fasces. It was created when the canton was formed in 1803.
origin: St. Gallen became a canton in 1803 under Napoleon's Act of Mediation. The fasces symbolised unity of the different territories joined together. The design was redrawn in 2011.

colors.name: Green
colors.meaning: Freedom, a colour popular in the Helvetic Republic era.

symbols.name: Fasces
symbols.description: A bundle of rods bound around an axe.
symbols.meaning: Unity and strength of the joined districts.

facts: The fasces is a Roman symbol of authority.
The Abbey of St Gall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
clues: A white bundle of rods with an axe on green.
A canton created in 1803 under Napoleon.
